paragraphs: Art. 2. (1) The property of the state is public and private.
(2) Public state property is:
1. the objects and properties under Art. 18(1) of the Constitution, declared by law to be exclusive state property;
2. the objects and properties declared public state property by law or by an act of the Council of Ministers;
3. the movable things declared public state property by law or by an act of the Council of Ministers;
4. the properties given to state bodies for the exercise of their functions;
5. the properties of national importance, intended for the lasting satisfaction of public needs of national importance through common use, set by the Council of Ministers;
6. the regulated land plots designated for the border checkpoints, and the buildings built on them.

(3) Private state property is all other properties and things that belong to the state. The fruits and the income of properties and things that are public state property are private property of the state.

(4) The properties and things of commercial companies and of non-profit legal entities are not state property within the meaning of this act, even if the state was the only owner of the property transferred to them.
Art. 5. (1) The state certifies the creation, the change and the end of its right of ownership of properties with an act of state property.
(2) The act of state property is an official document made by an official in the procedure and form set by law.
(3) The act of state property has no constitutive effect.
Art. 6. (1) Properties and things that are public state property and have lost that quality are declared private state property by a decision of the Council of Ministers.
(2) Properties and things that are private state property are declared public state property by a decision of the Council of Ministers.
(3) The objects and properties of exclusive state property cannot be declared private state property.
Art. 7. (1) Properties and things that are public state property cannot be the object of disposal and cannot be acquired by prescription.
(2) (Repealed.)

(3) Properties and things that are private state property can be the object of disposal and can be acquired by prescription. The Property Act applies to them, as far as this act does not provide otherwise.
(4) The ownership of properties that are public state property is not subject to restitution.

(5) In the cases and under the conditions set by law, limited real rights may be created by a decision of the Council of Ministers on properties of exclusive and public state property when this is necessary for:
1. the construction of a national object;
2. the lasting satisfaction of public needs;

3. the construction of linear objects of technical infrastructure outside items 1 and 2, when there is no other technical possibility or another technical solution is clearly not economically reasonable.
(6) The limited real rights under para. 5 cannot be created on public state properties connected with national security and defence.
Art. 43. (1) The state may acquire properties by purchase, exchange, gift, partition, creation of real rights for value or free of charge, will or other ways set by law.

(2) The state disposes of properties that are private state property, on valuations by an independent valuer not lower than their tax assessments, by sale, exchange, partition, creation of limited real rights for value or free of charge, and by contribution of properties and things to the capital of commercial companies.
(3) (Repealed.)

(4) The state enterprises under Art. 62(3) of the Commerce Act may dispose of private state properties acquired by or given to them with the permission of the minister who exercises the rights of the state, under the conditions and procedure of the implementing regulations. When the tax assessment of the property or the building right is above 500,000 лв., the disposal is made by that minister after a decision of the Council of Ministers.

Art. 44. (1) The sale of properties that are private state property with a tax assessment above 10,000 лв. is made by the Agency for Public Enterprises and Control under the Privatisation and Post-Privatisation Control Act. The electronic platform under Art. 3a(1) of that act is used for the sale.

(2) The sale of properties that are private state property with a tax assessment up to 10,000 лв. is made by the regional governor of the property's location, under the conditions and procedure of the act and its implementing regulations. The regional governor uses the electronic platform under Art. 3a(1) of the Privatisation and Post-Privatisation Control Act for the sale.

(3) Outside the cases under paras. 1 and 2 and Art. 43(2) and (4), the sale of land, or of ideal parts of land, that is private state property to persons who own a lawfully built building on it is made by the regional governor of the property's location without an auction, under the implementing regulations. The price is set under the implementing regulations.

Art. 48. (1) The disposal of properties that are private state property, except the sale under Art. 44(1), is made by an order of the regional governor, and in the cases under Art. 45(4) and Art. 47(2), of the Minister of Regional Development and Public Works. A contract is concluded on the basis of the order.

(2) The contracts by which the state acquires properties and disposes of properties that are private state property are concluded in written form and are entered on the order of the registration judge of the property's location.
Art. 68. (1) Acts of state property are drawn up for the properties that are state property.
(2) The Minister of Regional Development and Public Works approves separate forms of acts of state property for exclusive, public and private state properties.
(3) Acts of state property are also drawn up for properties of the Bulgarian state abroad.
(4) No acts of state property are drawn up for temporary structures, the road network and the beds of rivers and ravines, unless a special law provides otherwise.

Art. 70. (1) Acts of public and private state property are drawn up in two copies by the "State Property" unit of the regional governor. They are signed by the official who draws them up and approved by the regional governor. The two copies are presented to the registry office within 14 days of the approval, and after the entry the first copy is kept in the "State Property" unit. Copies are given to the Ministry of Regional Development and Public Works and to the persons who use the property after the entry.

(2) Acts of state property for properties connected with classified information that is a state secret, or with the security and defence of the country, are drawn up in two copies by the "State Property" unit of the ministry or body that manages the property, signed by the official who draws them up and approved by the minister or the head of the body. The first copy is kept in that ministry or body, the second is sent to the Ministry of Regional Development and Public Works, and a copy to the regional governor. Separate registers are kept for these acts.

(3) Acts of state property for properties of the Bulgarian state abroad are drawn up in the Ministry of Finance in three copies on a form approved by the Minister of Regional Development and Public Works, signed by the official who draws them up and approved by the Minister of Finance. The copies are kept in the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Regional Development and Public Works and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and a copy is sent to the user of the property.
(4) The documents that establish the state's right of ownership are attached to the acts of state property.
